title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Risk Warning for Civil Litigation in the People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Risk Warning for Civil Litigation of the People's Courts"

Fa Fa [2003] No. 25

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the Intermediate People's Courts of all separately planned cities:

In order to implement the important thought of "Three Represents," to implement the judicial measures for the people proposed by the Supreme People's Court, to further facilitate the people's access to litigation, to promote the parties' exercise of their litigation rights and performance of corresponding litigation obligations in accordance with law, to avoid adverse adjudicative consequences arising from improper exercise of rights or performance of obligations, and to fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, the Supreme People's Court, on the basis of summarizing the experience of litigation risk warnings of people's courts at all levels and fully soliciting opinions from all sectors of society, has formulated the unified text of the "Risk Warning for Civil Litigation of the People's Courts" (hereinafter referred to as the "Risk Warning") for uniform application by people's courts at all levels nationwide. On December 23, 2003, the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court discussed and approved the text of the "Risk Warning" at its 1302nd meeting, which is hereby published. To give full play to the role of the "Risk Warning" in facilitating and protecting the people, the following matters are hereby notified:

1. Pay attention to publicity work. The civil litigation risks contained in the "Risk Warning" are the legal consequences arising from a party's improper exercise of litigation rights or performance of litigation obligations as stipulated by current civil laws and judicial interpretations, and are not new civil litigation risks created by the "Risk Warning." The purpose of warning parties of litigation risks is to enable them to prudently exercise their litigation rights and actively perform their litigation obligations, thereby avoiding adverse adjudicative consequences arising from improper exercise of rights or performance of obligations. People's courts at all levels shall do a good job in publicity.

2. Pay attention to explanation work. Although the "Risk Warning" uses as plain language as possible, there are still some legal terms that are difficult for parties to understand. In order to enable parties to correctly understand the precise meaning of the provisions of the "Risk Warning," people's courts at all levels shall patiently explain them, so as to implement the judicial measures for the people.

3. Ensure the printing of the unified text of the "Risk Warning." Starting from January 1, 2004, the "Risk Warning" used by people's courts at all levels shall be the unified text approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court. The printing of the text shall be arranged by each higher people's court according to local circumstances; it may be uniformly printed by the higher people's court, or printed by people's courts at various levels themselves.

The "Risk Warning" is hereby issued to you. Please organize its implementation and execution carefully in light of actual work. If any problems arise during implementation, please promptly report them to this Court.

December 24, 2003

Risk Warning for Civil Litigation of the People's Courts

To facilitate the people's access to litigation and help parties avoid common litigation risks and reduce unnecessary losses, the common risks in civil litigation are hereby warned as follows, in accordance with the provisions of the "General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China," the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," and the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Litigation" and other laws and judicial interpretations:

1. Filing a lawsuit that does not meet the conditions

If a party files a lawsuit that does not meet the conditions prescribed by law, the people's court will not accept it, and if accepted, will dismiss the action.

If a party files a lawsuit that does not comply with the jurisdictional provisions, the case will be transferred to the people's court with competent jurisdiction for trial.

2. Inappropriate claims

The claims raised by a party shall be clear, specific, and complete. The people's court will not adjudicate claims not raised.

The claims raised by a party shall be appropriate; do not arbitrarily expand the scope of claims. Groundless claims, in addition to not being supported by the people's court, will also result in the party bearing the corresponding litigation costs.

3. Changing claims beyond the time limit

If a party adds or changes claims or files a counterclaim beyond the time limit permitted or designated by the people's court, such claims may not be adjudicated.

4. Exceeding the statute of limitations

The period during which a party may request the people's court to protect civil rights is generally two years (one year for special cases). After the plaintiff files a lawsuit with the people's court, if the defendant argues that the plaintiff's lawsuit has exceeded the legal protection period, and the plaintiff fails to provide evidence to prove the fact that the legal protection period has not been exceeded, the plaintiff's claims will not be supported by the people's court.

5. Unclear authorization

Where a party entrusts an agent ad litem to perform matters such as admitting, waiving, or changing claims, reaching a settlement, filing a counterclaim or appeal, such matters shall be specifically indicated in the power of attorney. If the special authorization matters are not clearly and specifically stated in the power of attorney, the opinions expressed by the agent ad litem on the aforementioned special authorization matters shall have no legal effect.

6. Failure to pay litigation fees on time

If a party, when filing a lawsuit or appeal, fails to prepay litigation fees on time, or fails to pay litigation fees after applying for deferment, reduction, or exemption of payment without approval, the people's court will rule that the lawsuit or appeal is deemed to be withdrawn automatically.

If a party files a counterclaim but fails to prepay the corresponding case acceptance fee in accordance with regulations, the people's court will not adjudicate it.

7. Application for property preservation not in compliance with regulations

If a party applies for property preservation but fails to pay the preservation fee as required, the people's court will not take preservation measures against the property subject to the application for preservation.

If a party files an application for property preservation but fails to provide corresponding property guarantee as required by the people's court, the people's court will dismiss the application according to law.

If the applicant's application for property preservation is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for the losses suffered as a result of the property preservation.

8. Failure to provide evidence or insufficient provision of evidence

Except as otherwise provided by law and judicial interpretations that no evidence is required to prove, a party who raises a claim or refutes the other party's claim shall provide evidence to prove it. Failure to provide corresponding evidence or to prove the relevant facts with the evidence provided may result in adverse adjudicative consequences.

9. Providing evidence beyond the time limit for evidence

Evidence submitted by a party to the people's court shall be submitted within the time limit agreed upon by the parties and approved by the people's court or designated by the people's court. Evidence submitted beyond the aforementioned time limit may be deemed by the people's court as the party having waived the right to adduce evidence, except for new evidence as provided by law and judicial interpretations.

10. Failure to provide original evidence

Where a party provides evidence to the people's court, it shall provide the original or the original object; under special circumstances, copies or reproductions verified by the people's court as being identical to the originals may also be provided. If the evidence provided does not meet the above conditions, it may affect the probative force of the evidence, and may even be inadmissible.

11. Witness failing to testify in court

Except in special circumstances where a witness truly has difficulty appearing in court as provided by law and judicial interpretations, if a party provides witness testimony, the witness shall appear in court to testify and undergo cross-examination. If the witness fails to appear in court to testify, it may affect the evidentiary effect of the witness testimony, and may even be inadmissible.

12. Failure to apply for audit, appraisal, or assessment in accordance with regulations

If a party applies for audit, appraisal, or assessment but fails to file the application within the time limit designated by the people's court, or fails to prepay the audit, appraisal, or assessment fees, or fails to provide relevant materials, resulting in the inability to determine the disputed facts through audit, appraisal, or assessment conclusions, it may produce adverse adjudicative consequences for the applicant.

13. Failure to appear in court on time or withdrawing from court during proceedings

If the plaintiff, after being summoned by summons, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or withdraws from court during the proceedings without the permission of the court, the people's court will deem the lawsuit to be withdrawn automatically; if the defendant files a counterclaim, the people's court will render a default judgment on the contents of the counterclaim.

If the defendant, after being summoned by summons, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or withdraws from court during the proceedings without the permission of the court, the people's court will render a default judgment.

14. Failure to provide accurate service address

In cases tried under the summary procedure, when the people's court serves litigation documents to the address for service provided by the party themselves, if the address provided by the party is inaccurate, or if the party changes the address for service without timely notifying the people's court, resulting in the inability of the people's court to serve the documents and causing the return of the litigation documents, the litigation documents shall be deemed to have been served.

15. Applying for compulsory enforcement beyond the time limit

The time limit for applying to the people's court for compulsory enforcement is one year if both parties or one party is a citizen, and six months if both parties are legal persons or other organizations. The time limit shall be calculated from the date on which the performance obligation determined by the effective legal document expires. If the application is filed beyond the aforementioned time limit, the people's court will not accept it.

16. No property or insufficient property available for enforcement

If the person subject to enforcement has no property or insufficient property to fulfill the obligations determined by the effective legal document, the people's court may rule to suspend enforcement for the unfulfilled portion, and the property rights and interests of the applicant for enforcement may be temporarily unrealizable or not fully realizable.

17. Failure to perform obligations determined by effective legal documents

If the person subject to enforcement fails to perform the obligation to pay money within the period specified in the effective legal document, the person shall pay double the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance.

If the person subject to enforcement fails to perform other obligations within the period specified in the effective legal document, the person shall pay a surcharge for delayed performance.
